original_card.question: Does one changed supplier or assembly claim lack a source-bound independent check of a specific new implication?
methods: Independently reconstruct a coordinated frame/circuit change and its single-change control, then derive the complete rank and physical ledger.
Implement certified moment inequalities through a different exact enclosure method.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Demonstrate independence, source binding, positive cases and semantic failure controls. Name the existing checks and the missing coverage. More digits or another equivalent evaluation of an unchanged root is not by itself new verification coverage.

first_step.inspect: Read #2979 joint rank-7 end-frame proposal and the revision-6 evidence status. Its claimed kappa is not selected. Compare coordinated changes with the losing single-change controls and locate the complete physical ledger; an aggregate moment alone does not validate the mechanism.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Prioritize a bounded independent audit of #2979: reconstruct one joint group and its single-lowering control, check the declared frames/chronology, then trace changed children, idle widths and cleanup buffers into the complete invoice and both supplier caps. Choose one still-missing implication after checking existing audits. Stop with exact unresolved dependencies if full admission exceeds the session; do not launch a new lowering census on an unvalidated premise or substitute extra root digits for mechanism checking.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Independent pricing prevents unsupported frontier claims and can reveal genuine accounting slack.
allowed_variations: Reconstruct either a source ledger or a numeric enclosure with a different method.
scope_change_triggers: Importing the primary function and calling its output independent verification.
Promoting #2979 from merged source archive to validated supplier solely from author PASS receipts or aggregate pricing.

actual_scope: PR3605 (head 3efbb5de) staged helpers 644 and 660 only: bind their emitted native entering wrappers, climbs, FULL exit adapters and direct scalar clocks to the source words in both orientations and both providers, and check the shared span(429,30)->FULL width-7 residual and every climb recipe on all 512 Gaussian columns with Sagar Thakrar's separately written kernel (no bw_* code in the identity check). The parent PR3133 words through the same producer are the single-change control. Extension: the same binding and kernel check on the consumer words that retime the 644/660 releases, RETIMED644-660 (#3642 head 6568db75, byte-identical in #3653 head 607a09ff) and DELAYED (#3682 head 431e6c60), with PR3605's STAGED words as the single-change control, each regenerated emission bound to the producing PR's recorded LOCAL-CHECKS receipt.
scope_change_reason: The card's first experiment targets #2979, whose four rank-7 groups already have native residual audits (group A, #3411 group B, the group-C package, group D). The live #2979-descendant line (PR3605 and the consumers that reuse its STAGED words: #3624, #3626, #3630, #3633, #3638) changes exactly one native residual, the span(429,30) entrance of ordinary FULL helpers 644/660. PR3687 checked those words as free-operator identities and left the native phases of this entrance as its open question 1, asking for a check without the bw_* lineage code. This package answers that one question. The extension answers the package's own first open question: the retimed (#3642/#3653) and delayed (#3682) consumers use different words, so the check covers them only if those words keep the same native entrance.
bottleneck_link: The whole 8->7 width saving of PR3605 rests on the native wrapper identity for span(429,30), and every listed consumer inherits it. A width saving that the native residual does not realize would cancel the consumers' conditional gains.
stop_rule: Finish the finite native binding and separate-kernel identity for helpers 644/660 in the STAGED, RETIMED and DELAYED words, with the parent PR3133 and STAGED single-change controls. No owner journal, release, root or kappa work; record any changed entrance or recipe as a finding; stop at a source mismatch or a failed identity.
evidence: RESULT.json via verify.py: for both providers and both orientations, helpers 644/660 have one pre/post residual wrapper pair at frame span(429,30) with no terminal field, one new_to_old exit adapter at FULL, no private buffer, and climbs [2,1,2,1,1] / [2,2,1,1,1] summing to 7; all 17 direct scalar clocks per helper match the source word. The shared recipe (key 137) satisfies L*F_7*R = T_FULL*T_E^-1 (operator order, rightmost first) phase-exactly on all 512 columns under the separate kernel; the wrapped and inverse-transpose forms, which follow from it, are also evaluated. Ten distinct climb recipes also pass. The parent PR3133 words give width 8 with first climbs 3 instead of 2, every climb ending at the same frame; only 644/660 change entrance/terminal pairs. Serialized residual recipes go 56 -> 57; pair classes go 57 -> 58, counting the unwrapped cold class ([], FULL). Seven residual controls per provider are rejected: three at the all-column operator check (global phase, parent right-wrapper alias, wrong plane [429,18]) and four at the width check. Consumers: for RETIMED644-660 (#3642, reused byte for byte by #3653) and DELAYED (#3682), both providers and both orientations, the LF-form regenerated LOCAL-CHECKS.json equals the producing PR's recorded receipt (11743473... and 7ff1aabb...); the reconstructed residual-adapter file equals the STAGED one (all 57 recipes and 72 warp records); no helper changes its entrance/terminal pair; 644/660 keep key 137, the span(429,30) wrapper pair, the FULL exit adapter and the STAGED climb frames and ranks, and the width-7 recipe passes the separate kernel; all 17 direct scalar clocks per helper match the consumer word, and binding the STAGED word to a consumer program is rejected. The first climb moves B1045->B592 and B1085->B642 (RETIMED) or B1045->B1043 and B1085->B1084 (DELAYED). Only donors 640/656 change climbs, [1,2,2,1,1,1] -> [3,2,1,1,1], and both merged climb recipes span(30)->span(423,65,20,10) and span(30)->span(427,96,24,6) pass the separate kernel. The LOCAL-CHECKS digest is now taken in LF form (bw_emit.py writes CRLF on Windows), which makes the receipt platform-independent. test_verify.py: 8 tests; emitted-stream, recipe, word, pin and consumer-comparison corruptions are rejected, each consumer corruption at its own check. Local-only (not registered): the producer's own bw_adapters.py under Python 3.13.1 and numpy 2.2.2 writes a RESIDUAL-ADAPTERS.json whose LF-normalized bytes equal this package's reconstruction for both providers.

open_questions.question: Do all 57 serialized residual recipes and all 72 warp records (240 emitted warp events) of the staged words pass the separate kernel, not only the changed recipe?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package checks the one residual recipe that PR3605 changes; the other 56 are inherited from the PR3133 parent and rely on the bw_gauss lineage check or earlier group audits. The STAGED, RETIMED and DELAYED adapter files are identical, so one run covers all three word families.
open_questions.first_step: Loop check_recipe over every key of the reconstructed adapter file and check each warp K record as a monomial identity with the same kernel; record the runtime.
open_questions.blocked_by: Not attempted; it extends coverage rather than answering PR3687's open question.

open_questions.question: Does the complete emitted 644/660 lane, including scalar macros and the warps of their partners, realize the free-operator identity phase-exactly under an independent simulator?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Correct wrapper and climb recipes do not by themselves prove that the emitted scalar macros between them are phase-exact; PR3605 checks that with the inherited bw_phases stage. For the consumers it would also check natively that the moved releases commute with the gates they cross, which this package binds only as emission clocks.
open_questions.first_step: Simulate the emitted forward stream on basis inputs supported on the 644/660 lanes with the separate kernel's Gaussian state and compare with the free-operator endpoint from PR3687.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs an independent emitted-event interpreter for scalar macros and warps, which neither this package nor the group audits provide.

open_questions.question: Which open PRs carry 644/660 words that differ from the STAGED, RETIMED and DELAYED bytes checked here?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package covers exactly six words (three families, two providers); a consumer that vendors further-edited words is not covered until it passes the same comparison.
open_questions.first_step: List the blob ids of *644-660*.json.gz and DELAYED-*.json.gz files across open PR heads with git ls-tree, and run the consumer comparison (common.CONSUMERS plus a pin) on any new bytes.
open_questions.blocked_by: Not attempted; only #3642, #3653 and #3682 were fetched for this extension.
